svg.title: Tangential variables remain parameters. This depends only on normal jets through m along N⊥ g and vanishes for tests supported away from that subspace. Its support lies in {x : x −πgx ∈ supp f, ∥πgx∥≤2s}. For orthogonal normals projections annihilate each other, derivatives com- mute and cutoffs use separate variables; Taylor and remainder operators therefore commute for disjoint groups. These facts follow directly from the displayed derivative formula and the cutoff. For input degrees dj, define ωg = P j∈g dj and Lg = max(0, ωg +1−νg). Resolve the expression into degrees h = 0, . . . , Lg −1 and its remaining component using the fixed field reader. Pair the remaining component with f, and the projected degree-h term with the normal remainder through Lg −1 −h. For these finite choices v, gains are Gv = Lg and Gv = h respectively; after normal integration, ev = νg + Gv −ωg. (CE3)
